body.purpose: Page-level sentences, 13px Archivo; measure capped at 64-68ch.

reasoning.purpose: Agent reasoning sentences printed into decision lines.

micro.purpose: Column heads, nav, tokens, buttons: mono caps, 0.12em tracking.

data.purpose: References, PO numbers, dates, confidences: mono, tabular numerals.

amount.purpose: Money on a slip: 18px mono, used once per record.

motion.name: print-in
motion.purpose: A decision line printing into its fixed cell. The one authored motion moment.

motion.name: lamp-pulse
motion.purpose: An unacknowledged change on a row or the nav lamp.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Hover, focus and border changes on controls; never longer than 250ms.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Kill switch for both keyframe animations.

narrative.overview: InvoiceFlow's queue is not a dashboard of KPI cards; it is a register of confirmations. The product's whole claim is that every decision an agent made is readable after the fact, so the interface is built like the paperwork that has always carried trust in accounts payable: a pale print ground, an ink-green shell, hairlines that separate one record from the next, and confirmation lines printed into fixed cells in the order they happened. The register refuses the category default twice: no hero metric grid, and no decision summarised into a coloured pill. A disposition is a stamped token with a square swatch, the way a clerk would stamp a slip.
keyCharacteristics: Print-and-ink world: pale #f2f2ea ground, ink-green shell, 1px rules instead of card shadows.
Two voices: Archivo sets labels and prose; Sometype Mono sets every reference, amount, timestamp, confidence and token.
Dispositions are stamps, never pills, and colour only ever means state.
Density for a clerk working a queue all day: 36px rows, tabular numerals, no wasted verticals.
Motion conveys state only: the print-in cascade on new decision lines and a lamp pulse for unacknowledged changes.

rules.name: The Registers, Not Dashboards Rule
rules.body: A screen in this product is a ruled record with a fixed reading order. If an arrangement could belong to any SaaS dashboard, it is wrong here.

rules.name: The Stamp Rule
rules.body: State is shown as a stamped mono token with a square swatch beside it. Pills, dots alone, and colour blocks without a word are not dispositions.

rules.name: The Monospace Means Data Rule
rules.body: Sometype Mono appears only where a value must be compared column-to-column or read back verbatim. Prose is always Archivo.

rules.name: The Two Jobs Rule
rules.body: Colour either states a disposition or marks something unacknowledged. Nothing is coloured for decoration, importance, or category.

rules.name: The Fixed Cell Rule
rules.body: Numeric columns are right-aligned mono with tabular numerals so digits line up down the register; a proportional face in a numeric column is a defect.

rules.name: The Layered Paper Rule
rules.body: To lift something, put it on a brighter paper and rule its edge. Never float it with a shadow, a blur, or a backdrop filter.

dos: Do keep one reading order per record: what happened, how sure, which rule.
Do print reasoning sentences verbatim from the audit table; never paraphrase them in the UI.
Do reserve colour for state and for the unacknowledged lamp.
Do use tabular mono for anything that is compared or read back.
Do give every control default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled and loading states.
donts: Don't build a KPI card grid, a big-number hero, or an eyebrow above a heading.
Don't put a decision in a pill, a dot alone, or a coloured left border.
Don't add shadows, glass, blur, gradient text, or decorative progress rings.
Don't use mono as a costume outside data: no mono paragraphs, no mono headings.
Don't claim compliance or payment execution anywhere in the interface; this build does neither.
